extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators and curriculum designers (K-12 through university)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing mathematics courses that foreground and develop 'mathematical habits of mind' alongside traditional content, with concrete habits (algebraic, analytic) and pedagogical practices to cultivate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make mathematical thinking a key concept in the syllabus
rubrics_metrics.description: Make mathematical thinking a key concept in the syllabus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat mathematical thinking itself as an explicit learning target in the course syllabus rather than only listing topics or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about one's own thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about one’s own thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model thought processes for students so they see how a mathematician reasons, not just the polished final answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work on problems with students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in joint problem solving rather than only presenting solutions; let students see problem-solving in progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make thought experiments an integral part of the experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Make thought experiments an integral part of the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include visualization and imagination tasks (e.g., visualize solids of revolution; picture calculations like (x−1)(x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1); imagine change) so students practice mental experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience before formality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide students with experiences and activities before immediately presenting the formal theorem or definition; allow time for student activity/thought to cement and clarify transitions from example/process to concept (Tony Gardiner’s critique of typical university lectures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Look to the mathematics itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Look to the mathematics itself — traditional branches are descriptors for the habits of mind indigenous to that discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the character of mathematical subfields (analysis, algebra, arithmetic, geometry, topology) to inform which habits of mind to cultivate in instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting regularity from calculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage students to detect patterns in computation (e.g., difference tables) and to abstract general rules or polynomial behavior from sequences of values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking structural similarities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach students to recognize when different problems share the same algebraic structure (example: polynomial interpolation vs. simultaneous congruences/Chinese remainder), and to transfer solution ideas across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension (algebraic habit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the habit of extending definitions or operations to broader domains (e.g., extending arithmetic notions to polynomial rings) as an algebraic strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition (algebraic habit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice breaking objects or problems into simpler components as an approach to algebraic reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation (algebraic habit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize multiple representations (symbolic, numeric, structural) and how representation choices reveal structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization (algebraic habit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop sensitivity to working 'locally' (in a substructure or modulo a divisor) as a problem-solving tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction (algebraic habit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reducing complex problems to previously solved or simpler cases as a deliberate strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning by continuity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster habits that use continuity arguments (e.g., intermediate value-type reasoning: was there a time height equaled weight? is there a line cutting area in half?) to make existence or comparison arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by continuity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the habit of extending definitions plausibly via continuity (e.g., defining fractional or negative exponents, limits, or irrational values) and discussing reasonable definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking at extreme cases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use testing of extreme or boundary cases to probe conjectures, definitions, and the robustness of solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using approximation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach approximation as a strategy: approximate complicated objects/problems to gain insight and guide rigorous work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing to the limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reasoning that uses limiting processes as a legitimate method of argument and definition (e.g., sequences, integrals, continuity limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed pattern recognition in context and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns need to have 'meaning'. Experience of 'patterns' needs always to be embedded in a 'context' and to be accompanied by some form of 'interpretation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unanchored 'pattern sniffing'—require learners to ground observed patterns in context and rudimentary theories that provide interpretation and criteria for belief in patterns (quoting Glenn Stevens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance habits of mind with content and connections
rubrics_metrics.description: This is not to say that other facets of mathematics should be neglected; questions of content, applications, cultural significance, and connections are all essential in the design of a mathematics program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While prioritizing mathematical ways of thinking, also attend to factual content, applications, cultural relevance, and interconnections so students receive a well-rounded program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make explicit attention to mathematical ways of thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit attention to mathematical ways of thinking is necessary for intellectual sophistication and higher order thinking skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruction with deliberate learning goals around 'ways of thinking' (intellectual schemata) so students acquire transferable cognitive tools, not just procedural skills.
